subject: Information Theory
title: Biodiversity as Information
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Biodiversity as Information.

hook.text: Shannon's entropy formula was adopted by ecologists in 1949 to measure species diversity. Same math, different domain.

buildup.text: Shannon diversity index: H = -Σ pᵢ log pᵢ, where pᵢ is the proportion of species i. Higher H means more diverse.

discovery.text: A forest with 10 equally common species has higher Shannon diversity than one dominated by a single species.

twist.text: Ecologists use information theory daily, often without knowing its origin. Shannon's paper transformed biology too.

climax.text: Biodiversity loss reduces ecosystem information content, making systems less adaptable to environmental change.

punchline.text: Diversity is information. Species loss is data loss.

quiz.question: What does the Shannon diversity index measure?
